I have both the document explanation and the supporting data. Here's the answer:

## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

Per SOP-02 and the EQ-01 Reflow Oven Manual, a reflow oven in **standby draws 36% of its 70 kW rating — about 25.2 kW per oven** — for as long as it stays on, even though it produces nothing. That is a large idle load. A properly **switched-off** oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend. The rule is: ovens stay on for 30 minutes after the line stops, then must be switched off (only when no boards are inside) — never left in standby over the weekend or holidays. Idle energy from a standby oven is described as "the largest single source" of weekend idle energy. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

## Excess energy in incident S5

In incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), **RF-02 was left in standby all weekend**. The weekend energy was about **1,556 kWh** versus about **346 kWh** normal, an excess of about **1,210 kWh from a single oven**. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-02_weekend_shutdown.md#SOP-02 Weekend Shutdown > Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby]

The data confirms RF-02's heavy weekend draw: RF-02 consumed **2,310.3 kWh** over 17–20 October, the largest reflow-oven total of the three that period [data: get_energy]. Note the off-schedule rule only flags this after 120 minutes above 20% of rating, so the real benefit is preventing it before it happens.

Based on the demand-exceedance procedure, here is the answer:

## Load-shed order (shed first)

The **first load shed is the EV charging bank (EV-01)** — it is paused at 100%, because it has no effect on production and is the simplest action. [source: docs/knowledge/sop/SOP-03_demand_exceedance_response.md#SOP-03 Demand Exceedance Response > Step 2: shed in playbook order]

The full playbook order is:

| Order | Action | Equipment | Share of present load |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Pause EV charging** | EV-01 | 100% |
| 2 | Delay the next burn-in loading | BI-01, BI-02 | 35% |
| 3 | Raise chilled-water setpoint +1 °C | CH-01, CH-02 | 4% |
| 4 | Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar | AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 | 3.5% |

[source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

## Loads that must never be shed

These are never shed under any condition:
- **Server room (DC-01)**
- **Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04)**
- **Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03)**

[source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]

Note: I can only report the procedure and data — I cannot operate equipment, shed loads, or change settings myself.
